1.
This is a suit for perpetual injunction restraining use of trade mark "555", passing off, rendition of accounts etc. filed by the plaintiff.

2. The plaintiff has filed the above noted suit stating therein that the plaintiff is a partnership concern duly registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 and Shri Parveen Kumar is one of the partners of the plaintiff firm and is well Shri Virumal Praveen Kumar v. Gokal Chand Hari Chand conversant with the facts and circumstances of the case and is competent and authorized to sign, file, institute and verify the suit.

On account of continuous, regular and extensive use of the said trade mark "555" in respect of the said products of the plaintiff, the said mark has come to be associated with the plaintiff and none else.

sentences.text: The plaintiff is the first adopter, originator, author and owner of copyright in the said labels.

The trade mark "555" and the artistic label of the plaintiff is in relation to the products of the plaintiff have acquired secondary meaning and distinctiveness on account of long established,
continuous and extensive user coupled with large scale publicity throughout the country.
The trade mark "555" of the plaintiff was adopted to distinguish the products of the said goods of the plaintiff manufacture and is connected in the course of trade with the plaintiff exclusively.
The plaintiff has been spending substantial amount on publicity of the trade mark "555" and the annual sale of the said products run in several lacs of rupees.

The user of any identical and/or deceptively similar mark without consent of the plaintiff amounts to piracy of the said trade mark and the same is bound to cause confusion and deception in the course of trade and in the minds of unwary class of purchaser having imperfect recollection who are generally domestic servants and household ladies.

3. It is stated in the plaint that the defendants have been the distributors of the plaintiff's goods since the year 1991 and Shri Virumal Praveen Kumar v. Gokal Chand Hari Chand have been selling their goods under the trade mark "555" and a few months ago, the distributorship of the defendant was cancelled due to certain reasons.

sentences.text: When the products of the defendant came in the hands of the plaintiff, the plaintiff came to know that the defendant has also started marketing its products of buttons, safety pins under the similar trade mark "555" as those of the plaintiff.

The adoption and use of the said trademark"555" by the defendant for its products buttons and safety pins is an act of piracy of the plaintiff's mark and the defendant is also guilty of passing off its inferior quality goods as high quality goods of the plaintiff under the said trade mark of the plaintiff.
The defendant has no right or justification to adopt or use the impugned trade mark "555" which is identical and/or deceptively similar to the trade mark "555" of the plaintiff.
On account of defendant's aforesaid unlawful and unjust trade activity, the plaintiff has suffered in the well known and well established trade and reputation.

It is prayed that decree for perpetual injunction be passed thereby restraining the defendant, its servants, agents, representatives, dealers from selling or offering or exposing or advertising for sale or procuring to be sold, from passing off its inferior and substandard goods under the trade mark "555", also restraining the defendant Shri Virumal Praveen Kumar v. Gokal Chand Hari Chand from using the mark "555" and for delivery on affidavit by the defendant to the plaintiff all the offending, counterfeiting materials, labels, dies, blocks, containers etc. bearing the offending mark "555" under the possession and/or control of the defendant for destruction or for erasure purpose and for a decree for a sum of Rs.5,08,000/ in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant on account of defendant's illegal trade activities and for causing irreparable loss to the reputation and goodwill of the plaintiff alongwith cost of the suit.

My findings on the specific issues are as under:
11. Issue No.1:
The case of the plaintiff is that the plaintiff firm has been using trade mark "555" for its products of buttons, eyelets, fasteners, etc.
In para 5 of the plaint, the plaintiff has stated that they are lawful proprietor of the said trade mark "555" under the application No.555498 of the date of 30/07/1991 in class 26.
In para 11 of the plaint also, the plaintiff has stated that the plaintiff is a lawful owner of the impugned trade mark "555".
The plaintiff examined Shri Parveen Kumar as PW1 who adduced evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PX.
In para 5 of the affidavit Ex.PX, the PW1 stated that the plaintiff is the lawful proprietor of the said trade mark "555" under the application No.555498 of the date of 30/07/1991 in class 26.
Copy of the said application bearing No.555498 is Ex.PW1/4.

sentences.text: The contention of the defendant is that the plaintiff has been representing that the trade mark of the plaintiff is registered.

In the cross examination PW1 was confronted with carton/label Ex.PW1/D3 and PW1 admitted that vide this Shri Virumal Praveen Kumar v. Gokal Chand Hari Chand carton/label, the plaintiff represented his trade mark "555" with letters VR device swan (label) as registered under number 555498.

sentences.text: Thereafter, PW1 further voluntarily stated that he had got printed the trade mark number due to oversight under number 555498 and he did not repeat the said mistake in the subsequent labels.

It is to be noted that in the plaint, the plaintiff has only claimed that he is the lawful proprietor of the trade mark numerals "555" and they have applied for the registration of the same under application No.555498 of the date of 30/7/1991 in class 26.
PW1 admitted in the crossexamination that on account of oversight, they represented on their cartons Ex.PW1/D3 that their trade mark is registered but the same is not.
In the circumstances, it is held that the plaintiff is not registered proprietor of the trade mark numerals "555".
This issue stands answered accordingly.

Our Hon'ble High Court in case titled as Century Traders v. Roshan Lal Duggar & Co. reported in AIR 1978 Delhi 250 referred decision in Consolidated Foods Corporation v. Brandon and Co. Private Ltd., AIR 1965 Bom, 35 was wherein it was observed:

sentences.text: For the purpose of claiming such proprietorship of a mark, it is not necessary that the mark should have been used for considerable length of time.

Actual use of the mark under such circumstances as showing an intention to adopt and use it as a trade mark is the test rather than the extent or duration of the use.

A mere casual,
intermittent or experimental use may be insufficient to show an intention to adopt the mark as a trade mark for specific article or goods,......................."

24. In case titled as Goenka Institute of Education & Research v. Anjani Kumar Goenka & Anr.

sentences.text: The impugned judgment is incorrect to the extent it holds that user by the third party of a trademark prior to the user claimed by the plaintiff is not relevant.

In fact, in such a case, prior user by third parties of the trademark in certain facts and circumstances of a case may throw considerable light on, the existence or not, of exclusive ownership claim of a plaintiff/respondent with respect of a trademark.

It is to be noted that PW1 admitted in the cross examination that on carton Ex.PW1/D3, the plaintiff has mentioned encircled alphabet R and it has also mentioned trademark registration no.555498, although knowing very well that the trademark of the plaintiff is not registered.

It seems that the plaintiff deliberately used word registered on his carton Ex.PW1/D3 in order to create impression in the mind of public that it is trademark '555' which is registered one and also in order to deter other traders who are doing business in the same trade so that they do not use trademark '555' so that monopoly of the plaintiff is created in the trade mark '555'.

The plaintiff by using word registered trademark on Ex.PW1/D3, not only misled the public and other traders as also at the same time committed an offence which is punishable u/s 107 of The Trade Mark Act, 1999.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a suit for perpetual injunction restraining use of trade mark "555", passing off, rendition of accounts etc. filed by the plaintiff.
In para 4 of replication in reply to preliminary objections in Written Statement of defendant, the plaintiff has stated that the Suit No.2098/95 is pending before Hon'ble High Court.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The plaintiff is engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing of buttons, safety pins, hooks, eyelets, fastners etc. since the year 1989.
Since the year 1989 the plaintiff has been using the trade mark "555" for its products for the purpose of indicating or so as to indicate a connection in the course of trade between the said products and the plaintiff firm.
On account of continuous, regular and extensive use of the said trade mark "555" in respect of the said products of the plaintiff, the said mark has come to be associated with the plaintiff and none else.
People in the trade as well as general public consider the goods of the plaintiff under the trade Shri Virumal Praveen Kumar vs Gokal Chand Hari Chand on 30 January, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103597797/
1 mark "555" as the standard quality goods of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff is the lawful proprietor of the trade mark "555" under the application no. 555498 of the date 30.07.1991 in class 26 for the sale and marketing of its products.
The trade mark "555" and the artistic label of the plaintiff is in relation to the products of the plaintiff have acquired secondary meaning and distinctiveness on account of long established,
continuous and extensive user coupled with large scale publicity throughout the country.
The trade mark "555" of the plaintiff was adopted to distinguish the products of the said goods of the plaintiff manufacture and is connected in the course of trade with the plaintiff exclusively.
The user of any identical and/or deceptively similar mark without consent of the plaintiff amounts to piracy of the said trade mark and the same is bound to cause confusion and deception in the course of trade and in the minds of unwary class of purchaser having imperfect recollection who are generally domestic servants and household ladies.
The adoption and use of the said trademark"555" by the defendant for its products buttons and safety pins is an act of piracy of the plaintiff's mark and the defendant is also guilty of passing off its inferior quality goods as high quality goods of the plaintiff under the said trade mark of the plaintiff.
The defendant has no right or justification to adopt or use the impugned trade mark "555" which is identical and/or deceptively similar to the trade mark "555" of the plaintiff.
On account of defendant's aforesaid unlawful and unjust trade activity, the plaintiff has suffered in the well known and well established trade and reputation.
The plaintiff is using the trademark "VR"
device of SWAN with numerals "555" and the same are being marketed in a carton and the defendant is marketing spring snap fastners (tich buttons) under the trade mark ASIAN, device of dancing peacock with numerals "555" and as such the trade mark of the plaintiff as well as of the defendant are entirely different.
The use of the numerals "555" on the part of the plaintiff being tainted with piracy from the very beginning and they cannot be accorded protection of law and the plaintiff is not entitled to equitable relief of injunction.
